one_line: Nvidia's Jensen Huang returned as CEO amid government scrutiny and chip investigations, while US and European funding initiatives targeted AI infrastructure.

themes.title: Nvidia navigates leadership return and investigations
themes.text: Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia's CEO following lobbying by President Donald Trump and tech allies. The company faces ongoing investigations regarding chip smuggling to China, governance risks, and tighter US scrutiny over its financing arrangements.

themes.title: Infrastructure funding shifts amid new restrictions
themes.text: The European Union announced a €50 billion fund for AI and quantum companies, while the FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million Starmind AI satellite data centers. Meanwhile, new US chip restrictions halted billions in data center loans, and transaction data indicated that the AI Jevons paradox broke over a two-month period.

themes.title: Regulators challenge data sales and governance
themes.text: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general moved to block Character.ai from auctioning private chats from 21 million accounts. Additionally, India stressed human oversight for AI in conflicts at the UN, and the UN called for a global AI safety framework within a year.
